paper.title_en: Topological Geometry of Neutrino Mass and Mixing
paper.abstract_en: This work presents an analytical, parameter-free derivation of the lepton mixing matrix and active neutrino mass spectrum from an icosahedral $A_5$ flavor manifold coupled to the three-generation Iwahori-Hecke algebra $H_3(q)$. Partitioning the icosahedral vertex curvature across the six fundamental Weyl chambers of $H_3(q)$ fixes an elementary angular defect $Δ_{AD} = π/18$, unifying ultra-high-energy mass generation and low-energy flavor mixing as dual realizations of a single geometric invariant. At the topological braiding threshold $μ\sim M_0$, the right-handed Majorana scale $M_0$ breaks scale invariance and drives the five-dimensional Temperley-Lieb quotient into its hyperbolic regime with loop modulus $d'_{AD} = 2\coshΔ_{AD}$, where Quantum Yang-Baxter Baxterization projects the algebraic roots onto a hierarchical heavy spectrum $M_1 > M_2 > M_3 > 0$. Integrating out and inverting these states via a flavor-isotropic Seesaw mechanism Type-I locks in the normal mass hierarchy with $m_1 \approx 3.64$ meV, $\sum_i m_i \approx 63.5$ meV, and $m_β\approx 9.45$ meV. Simultaneously, probability conservation requires analytic continuation onto the compact unitary circle, factorizing the mixing matrix into the $A_5$ Golden Ratio baseline, a unitary boundary twist generated by the longest Coxeter involution, and a discrete Majorana parity matrix. This geometry yields $θ_{13} = 8.49^\circ$, $θ_{12} = 32.11^\circ$, $θ_{23} = 45^\circ$, and maximal Dirac CP violation, $δ_{CP} = \pm π/2$, while discrete $SO(3)$ parities quantize the relative Majorana phases, $α_{13} = -π, α_{23} = 0$, preventing $0νββ$ decay cancellation, $m_{ββ} \approx 1.14$ meV, and suppressing renormalization group drift to $\dotθ_{ij} \sim 10^{-7}$ rad.
